sentences.text:
Raj Kumar Verma, aged about 37 years, S/O Narayan Verma, r/o village Nimatand, PO - Sabalpur,
PS - Suryia, District- Giridih.
Petitioner  Versus  1. The State of Jharkhand.
2. Ishwar Prasad Kushwaha, s/o late Hari Mahto, r/o village Potma, PO & PS - Sariya, District- Giridih.
Opp. Parties  ------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Tarun Kr. No. 1, Advocate  For the State : Mr. Rajesh Kumar, Addl. P.P.

For the Opp. P. No. 2 : Mr. Krishna Shankar, Advocate ------
 PRESENT  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. with the prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding initiated against the petitioner in Protest cum Complaint Case No. 2750 of 2019 of the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:

1 3.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The brief fact of this case is that the petitioner sold his land to the complainant by executing sale deed and the mutation was done in the name of the complainant.
The complainant is paying land revenue receipt but the petitioner is not handing over the possession of the land sold to the complainant.

The complainant filed Complaint Case No. 140 of 2019 (2025:JHHC:36627) and the same was referred to Police under Section 156 (3) of the Cr.P.C. basing upon which Birni P.S. Case No. 16 of 2019 was registered.
After investigation, Police submitted Final Form against the petitioner on the ground that the dispute between the parties is a civil dispute and did not send the petitioner up for trial.

On the basis of the Protest cum Complaint Petition, statement of the complainant on solemn affirmation and the statement of the inquiry witnesses, the learned C.J.M.
vide order dated 03.08.2022 found prima facie case for the offences punishable under Sections 341 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner and directed to issue summons.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the trial of the case is yet to begin and charge has not yet been framed.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner relying upon the judgment of this Court in the case of Chandan Kumar Gupta & Another Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Another dated 27.06.2023 in Cr.M.P. No. 1221 of 2022 that in Para No. 8 therein, this Court has enumerated the essential ingredients of the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, which reads as under:-
"8.

entities.text: Chandan Kumar Gupta & Another Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Now, so far as the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code is concerned, the essential ingredients of the said offence are as follow:-
(i) Deception of a person either by making a false or misleading representation or by dishonest concealment or by any other act or omission, (2025:JHHC:36627)
(ii) Fraudulent or dishonest inducement of that person to either deliver any property or to consent to the retention thereof by any person or to intentionally induce that person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived and (iii) Such act or omission causing or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Mohammed Ibrahim & Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Anr.
reported in (2009) 8 SCC 751."

entities.text:
Mohammed Ibrahim & Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Anr.
reported in (2009) 8 SCC 751
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And submits that as none of the ingredients of the said offence is made out against the petitioner,
hence, the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out; even if the entire allegations made against the petitioner are considered to be true in their entirety.
6.
In this respect, learned counsel for the petitioner further relies upon the judgment passed by this Court in the case of Uma Devi & Others.

Vs. The State of Jharkhand reported in 2024: JHHC: 17102 Raj Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151810259/
2 and submits that in that case there was no allegation of impersonation against the petitioner of that case and this Court quashed the entire criminal proceeding.

entities.text: JHHC: 17102 Raj Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is lastly submitted that the prayer as prayed for in this criminal miscellaneous petition, be allowed.

7. Learned Addl. P.P. and the learned counsel for the Opposite Party No. 2 on the other hand vehemently oppose the contention of the petitioner and submits that the allegation against the petitioner is (2025:JHHC:36627) sufficient to constitute both the offences punishable under Sections 341 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
He further submits that the petitioner has not handed over the possession of the said land to the complainant.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit, be dismissed.

8. Having heard the submissions made at the bar and after going through the materials available on record, it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Uma Shankar Gopalika Vs. State of Bihar & Another reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336, Paragraph No. 6 of which reads as under: -
6. Xxxx xxxx

entities.text: Uma Shankar Gopalika Vs. State of Bihar & Another reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: xxxx It is well settled that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception.
If the intention to cheat has developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.

In the present case it has nowhere been stated that at the very inception there was any intention on behalf of the accused persons to cheat which is a condition precedent for an offence under Section 420 IPC."

(Emphasis supplied) that in order to constitute the offence punishable under 420 of the Indian Penal Code, it must be established that the accused has played deception since the beginning of the transaction between the parties and if the intention to deceive develops later on, the same will not amount to the offence of cheating.
9. Now coming to the facts of this case, the undisputed fact remains that the petitioner has sold his land by executing the sale deed and the land has been mutated in the name of the complainant.

Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner of playing deception since the beginning of the transaction between the parties and in the absence of essential ingredients, even if the entire allegations made against the parties are considered to be true in their entirety, still the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, is not made out.
10.

So far as the offence punishable under Section 341 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of N.S. Madhanagopal and Another vs. K. Lalithahas reported in 2022 0 Supreme (SC) 1243 laid down the essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under section 341 of the Indian Penal Code as follow:-
 "(i) there was obstruction by the accused;
 (ii) such obstruction prevented a person from proceeding in a direction Raj Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151810259/
3  to which he had a right to proceed and (iii) the accused caused such obstruction voluntarily.
(iv) The obstructor must intend or know or would have reason to believe that the means adopted would cause obstruction to the complainant."
11. Now coming to the facts of this case, there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner to obstruct any person or preventing any person from proceeding in any direction in which such person had the right to proceed.

entities.text: N.S. Madhanagopal and Another vs. K. Lalithahas reported in 2022 0 Supreme (SC) 1243
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Raj Kumar Verma vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of these essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under Section 341 of the Indian Penal Code, this (2025:JHHC:36627) Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegation made against the petitioner is considered to be true in its entirety, still the offence punishable under Section 341 of the Indian Penal Code, is not made out.

12. In view of the discussions made above, since neither of the two offences with respect to which prima facie case has been found by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate is made out against the petitioner, even if the entire allegation made in the complaint, statement of the complainant on solemn affirmation and statement of the inquiry witnesses are considered to be true in their entirety, hence, this Court is of the considered view that continuation of this criminal proceeding against the petitioner will amount to an abuse of the process of law.

13. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding against the petitioner in Protest cum Complaint Case No. 2750 of 2019 of the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih, is quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Protest cum Complaint Case No. 2750 of 2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 14. Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated the 04th December 2025 AFR/
